questions.qtext:
Consider the following $B^{+}$ tree structure where index blocks are identified as $\textbf{B1}$, $\textbf{B2}$, and $\textbf{B3}$, and the data entry blocks are $\textbf{B4}$ to $\textbf{B9}$.

For each of the following lookup operations, which blocks would be read and in which order? (Select all options that apply.)

options.text: Lookup record with key $\mathbf{41:\; B1 \rightarrow B3 \rightarrow B8}.$
Lookup records with keys in the range $\mathbf{2 0}$ to $\mathbf{3 0 :} \;\mathbf{B 1} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 3} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 6} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 7} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 8}$
Lookup records with keys in the range $\mathbf{2 0}$ to $\mathbf{3 0}: \mathbf{B 1} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 3} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 6} \rightarrow \mathbf{B 7}$

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B, C

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

Correct Answer: $\boxed{\textbf{A, B, and C}}$

  1. True: Key $41$ is in leaf $B8$. Path: $B1 \rightarrow B3 \rightarrow B8$
  2. True: Key $40$ would also be searched in $B8$, where we get to know that it does not exist
  3. True: The scan in leaves goes from $B6$ to $B8$
  4. False: Stopping at $B7$ is insufficient. It must read the next leaf $B8$ to verify that no keys in the range $[20,30]$ remain.

questions.qtext:
• The number d is the order of a $\mathrm{B}+$ tree. Each node (with the exception of the root node) must have $\mathrm{d} \leq \mathrm{x} \leq 2 \mathrm{~d}$ entries assuming no deletes happen (it's possible for leaf nodes to end up with $<\mathrm{d}$ entries if you delete data). The entries within each node must be sorted.
  • In between each entry of an inner node, there is a pointer to a child node. Since there are at most 2d entries in a node, inner nodes may have at most $2 \mathrm{~d}+1$ child pointers. This is also called the tree's fanout.
  • The keys in the children to the left of an entry must be less than the entry while the keys in the children to the right must be greater than or equal to the entry.
  • All leaves are at the same depth and have between d and 2d entries (i.e., at least half full)

Suppose we have an initially empty, order $\mathrm{d}=1 \ \mathrm{B}+$ tree, and the following set of keys:
$$\textbf{3,9,8,7,2,1,5,10,12}$$
Which of the following are possible B+ trees after inserting all of the above elements in some order? we follow the right branch when the split key equals the search key. When splitting a node with an odd number of keys, assume the new right node receives one more key than the original left node.
questions.solution:
Answer: C
